source_text:
Τοσοῦτον οὖν ἔλεος ποιήσαντος αὐτοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς, πρῶτον μέν, ὅτι ἡμεῖς οἱ ζῶντες τοῖς νεκροῖς θεοῖς οὐ θύομεν καὶ οὐ προσκυνοῦμεν αὐτοῖς, ἀλλὰ ἔγνωμεν δἰ αὐτοῦ τὸν πατέρα τῆς ἀληθείας: τίς ἡ γνῶσις ἡ πρὸς αὐτόν, ἢ τὸ μὴ ἀρνεῖσθαι δἰ οὖ ἔγνωμεν αὐτόν;
λέγει δὲ καὶ αὐτός: Τὸν ὁμολογήσαντά με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων. ὁμολογήσω αὐτὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πατρός μου.
οὗτος οὖν ἐστὶν ὁ μισθὸς ἡμῶν, ἐὰν οὖν ὁμολογήσωμεν δἰ οὖ ἐσώθημεν.
ἐν τίνι δὲ αὐτὸν ὁμολογοῦμεν; ἐν τῷ ποιεῖν ἃ λέγει καὶ μὴ παρακούειν αὐτοῦ τῶν ἐντολῶν, καὶ μὴ μόνον χείλεσιν αὐτὸν τιμᾶν, ἀλλὰ ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας.
λέγει δὲ καὶ ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ: Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἄπεστιν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ.
thought_title: Confessing Christ in deeds, not only with lips
orientation: The preacher has just said Christ saved many by coming and calling us while we were perishing; now he explains how believers should repay that mercy by confessing Christ through obedience and wholehearted honor, not mere lip-service.
pass_a_gloss: Since he has shown so great mercy to us, first, that we who are living do not sacrifice to dead gods and do not worship them, but we knew through him the Father of truth: what is the knowledge that is toward him, or the not denying him through whom we knew him? And he himself also says: The one who confessed me before men, I will confess him before my Father. This therefore is our reward, if therefore we confess him through whom we were saved. And in what do we confess him? In doing what he says and not disobeying his commandments, and not honoring him only with lips, but from the whole heart and from the whole mind. And he says also in Isaiah: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me.

choices.why: The participle with τοσοῦτον emphasizes the magnitude of the mercy already enacted toward us; 'shown' captures the active force of ποιήσαντος.
The dative plural with θύομεν and προσκυνοῦμεν marks the recipients of sacrifice and worship; 'dead gods' preserves the stark contrast with the living God.
The genitive τῆς ἀληθείας is rendered as a genitive of quality or source; 'Father of truth' is the standard literal rendering and matches the theological register.

choices.english: the knowledge that is toward him
choices.why: The preposition πρός with the accusative indicates direction or relation; 'toward him' preserves the relational sense of knowledge directed at God.
The articular infinitive with μή is a substantive expression; keeping the negation with the infinitive preserves the exact force of the question.
The articular infinitive with ἐν expresses the means or sphere of confession; 'in doing' keeps the instrumental sense.

bible_refs.note: Τὸν ὁμολογήσαντά με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁμολογήσω αὐτὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πατρός μου
Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἄπεστιν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ

pass_b_english: Since he has shown us such great mercy, think first of this: we who are alive do not sacrifice to dead gods or worship them. Through him we have come to know the Father of truth. And what is this knowledge of him? It is refusing to deny the one through whom we came to know him.
He himself says, "Whoever confesses me before men, I will confess him before my Father" (Matthew 10:32).
This, then, is our reward, if we confess the one through whom we were saved.
And how do we confess him? By doing what he says and not disobeying his commandments, and by honoring him not only with our lips but from our whole heart and from our whole mind.
For he says also in Isaiah, "This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me" (Isaiah 29:13).

last_rejected.why: Brief requires 'recompense' for μισθός/ἀντιμισθία; 'reward' is banned.
last_rejected.ruling: μισθός standardly means 'reward, pay, wages'; 'recompense' is a synonym, not required.

last_rejected.why: English 'He himself says' could imply Jesus, but source αὐτός refers back to 'the one through whom we came to know him'—God the Father or Christ? Context suggests Christ. However, the citation Matthew 10:32 is Jesus' words. The brief marks 'The Lord (Jesus)' as speaker for section 3. The English 'He himself says' is ambiguous; source 'αὐτός' with Christ as antecedent is clear. Actually this is probably fine.
last_rejected.ruling: λέγει δὲ καὶ αὐτός correctly rendered 'He himself says'; αὐτός refers to Christ, matching Matthew 10:32 citation.

last_rejected.source_quote: Τὸν ὁμολογήσαντά με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων. ὁμολογήσω αὐτὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πατρός μου
last_rejected.why: Source quotes Jesus' words matching Matthew 10:32 / Luke 12:8. The English correctly identifies Matthew 10:32. Not an error.
last_rejected.ruling: Quote matches Matthew 10:32 exactly; reference is correct.

last_rejected.why: Glossary does not cover 'διάνοια'; 'mind' is standard rendering. Not an error.
last_rejected.ruling: διανοίας rendered 'mind' is standard; no glossary issue reported as actual error.

polish.changed: Clarified the rhetorical question about knowledge, made the speaker of the Matthew quotation explicit, and broke the dense opening into shorter, more natural sentences while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.
